title: Apple GPU prefill 2x2 register ownership versus public rowwise
question: Does the EXP-0011 2x2 register mapping beat the public K-parallel rowwise kernel on the same rotating packed-QKV prefill workload, and where does their measured crossover begin?
hypothesis: At sufficiently large M, the 2x2 mapping's reuse across four outputs and elimination of one SIMD-group reduction per output may outweigh its four live accumulators, serial full-K work per lane, and smaller grid. The public rowwise mapping is expected to remain stronger near M=1 because it exposes K parallelism for every scalar output.

control.ownership: One SIMD group owns one scalar output. Its 32 lanes partition K=896, each lane accumulates 28 products, a SIMD-group sum combines the partials, and lane zero adds bias and stores.

candidate.ownership: One 32-lane SIMD group owns one 8x16 output tile. Each lane owns one 2x2 microtile, walks all K=896 values serially, and keeps four FP32 accumulators.

changed_mechanism: The complete arithmetic mapping changes: K-parallel collective ownership of one scalar output is compared with output-parallel ownership of one 8x16 tile and four outputs per lane. This necessarily changes grid shape, lane work, live accumulators, source-requested loads, reduction work, and generated code.
unchanged: BF16 input, weight, bias, and output with FP32 accumulation and one final BF16 cast
row-major X[M,K], W[N,K], and Y[M,N] layouts
zero threadgroup operand scratch and zero threadgroup barriers
one enqueue per layer and one completion boundary per measured workload
K=896, N=1152, and 24 distinct rotating weight allocations
no weight packing, quantization, shared K staging, Apple matrix primitive, or public dispatch change

correctness.authority: tests/test_linear.mojo plus each timed specialization's untimed exact-unit-output gate
required_cases: Existing public rowwise host-oracle, Qwen-width, decode, and prefill cases
Existing 2x2 candidate exact M=8 K=32 N=16 tile
Existing 2x2 candidate ragged M=9 K=129 N=17 tails
Existing 2x2 candidate Qwen-width M=8 K=896 N=128
Exact BF16 unit output at K=896 and N=1152 before timing every benchmark specialization
Existing direct and shared-staging experimental tests remain passing

workload_matrix.weights: 24 distinct allocations rotated once per measured workload iteration

measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: Within each block and M, 2x2-register median divided by public-rowwise median; summarize the four ratios with their median and retain every ratio.
measurement_protocol.environment: Clean immutable commit, AC power, no reported thermal or performance warning, Apple GPU plus Metal runtime identity, and MODULAR_DEBUG unset.

classification_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and 2x2-register faster in at least three of four blocks.
classification_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and 2x2-register slower in at least three of four blocks.

decision_rule.advance: Advance 2x2 as the manual prefill candidate only if it materially improves M=64, 128, and 256 against the public rowwise path.
decision_rule.reject: Reject this 2x2 mapping against public rowwise if it materially regresses M=64, 128, and 256.
decision_rule.crossover: Report the smallest tested candidate M in 8, 16, 32, and 64 from which no larger measured M materially regresses; separately report the stricter threshold from which every larger measured M materially improves.
decision_rule.otherwise: Make no advance or production change; retain the result as mixed or inconclusive.
decision_rule.production_decision: None. This comparison may qualify a manual candidate and characterize a crossover, but cannot change public dispatch by itself.

nonclaims: The comparison does not isolate register pressure, occupancy, K parallelism, output reuse, reduction cost, cache behavior, instruction scheduling, or compiler output individually.
Requested traffic is source-derived and is not observed hardware cache, fabric, or DRAM traffic.
A crossover in this bounded matrix does not by itself establish a production dispatch threshold.
A loss rejects this 2x2 shape for this workload, not all manual register tiles or hardware-matrix mappings.
No Apple matrix primitive, Neural Engine, tensor-core analog, end-to-end prompt, model, or decoder throughput result.
